Title: Corpus scriptorum historiae Byzantinae ... Pars XIX: Nicephorus Gregoras. Volumen II. Nicephori Gregorae Byzantina historia, Graece et Latine, cum annotationibus Hier. Wolfii, Car. Ducangii, Io. Boivini et Cl. Capperonnerii, cura Ludovici Schopeni
Creator: Nikephoros Gregoras (1295-1359 or 1360 per the host catalogue), Byzantine scholar and historian, an opponent of Palamas; Greek text edited, with Latin translation and notes, by Ludwig Schopen
Publisher: Bonn: Impensis Ed. Weberi, 1830 (Corpus scriptorum historiae Byzantinae)
Publication Date: 1830
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: the title page reads 'MDCCCXXX' (1830) in this scan's OCR (file line 173); host record: date 1829, possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT.
Language: grc (Greek with parallel or following Latin translation; the Latin and Greek share the OCR file; see the content note)
Source: Internet Archive item nicephorigregor02schogoog (archive.org/details/nicephorigregor02schogoog), full-text file nicephorigregor02schogoog_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the Library thread, October 2026.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the Library thread; the OCR text follows it unchanged. Nothing was stripped, normalised, corrected, re-spaced or retyped (the long s glyph occurs 0 times and was left as found). The Google Books boilerplate page at the head of the OCR is left in place. The file is 3061223 bytes, 2258134 characters and 57634 lines. OCR quality sampled at the title pages and at about 5%, 50% and 95% of the file (lines 2881, 28817 and 54752): Greek polytonic clean; Latin clean.
Content note: Volume 2 of the Bonn edition: Books XII to XXIV (the 1320s to 1351), which hold Gregoras's account of the Barlaam and Akindynos affair, the synods of 1341, 1347 and 1351 and his own breach with Palamas. Gregoras is the anti-Palamite witness whose side was condemned in 1351. Book numbers are given in the file (LIBER XII at line 213 to LIBER XXIV at 34827). Volume 3 (Books XXV-XXXVII) is vendored beside this one. Greek above, Latin below, with Boivin's and Capperonnier's notes.

18. φεύγοντα pro φεύγοντε positum esse observat Boiv. 


quem solum eundemque potentissimum adversarium consiliis suis fraudu- 
lentis obstare comperiebat, suo tamen more agere non desinebat. Inest 
enim illud opibus pariter et honoribus, ut cui indigno obvenerint, eius 
mentem non secus atque ebrietas ex sua sede dimoveant. Namque hic, 
cum ad honores et fortunae splendorem pervenisset , magnaque opum quae- 
sita vi suam excessisset sortem, decenti illico de statu animi declinavit,

fuit. Ergo etiam post hominem miserationis operatio fuit, ut et miseri- 
cordiae nomen. Magnus pariter Athanasius ita loquitur: ,,non verba na-
